info.title: CDMS API
info.description:
OpenAPI specification for the REST APIs that CRScube CDMS exposes externally
through its API gateway.

This document covers the public integration APIs for CDMS.

## Scope

| Area | Operations | Tag |
|------|-----------:|-----|
| CRF data upload | 1 | `crf` |
| Dataset extraction | 4 | `dataset` |
| Subject registration | 1 | `subject` |
| Central Lab | 5 | `central-lab` |

## How to read the status codes

There are several places where HTTP status codes are used differently from what
you would expect. Review this table before you integrate.

| Situation | Actual response | Expected |
|-----------|-----------------|----------|
| CRF server-side processing failure | **200** + `result: false` | 5xx |
| No study access permission for CRF | **200** + `(2200)` | 403 |
| Extraction in progress / download not ready | **202** + `status: fail` | 409 |
| Resource not found (`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`) | **400** | 404 |
| No permission (`FORBIDDEN`) | **400** | 403 |
| Internal dataset error (`INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`) | **400** | 500 |
| Central Lab FileKey missing | **401** | 404 |
| Central Lab data buffer exceeded | **413** | 400 |
| Duplicate screening number (`CONFLICT`) | 409 | 409 |

**Never treat 2xx as success on its own.** Failures arrive with 200 and 202.

401, 403, 404, 500 and 504 are returned by **the gateway**. Only the CRF
endpoint delivers those errors in the `ApiResponse` format; everything else
uses `GatewayFailResponse`.

## Response formats

| Response format | Structure | Used by |
|-----------------|-----------|---------|
| `ApiResponse` | `{txId, result, error{message, errors}}` | CRF, and gateway errors on CRF |
| `SuccessResponse` / `FailResponse` | `{status, result}` / `{status, message, error{errorCode, errorDetails}}` | dataset GET |
| `ExternalSuccessResponse` / `ExternalFailResponse` | the above plus `txId` | dataset POST, subject |
| `GatewayFailResponse` | `{txId, error{errorCode, errorDetails}, message, status}` | common gateway errors |
| `CentralLabFailResponse` | same shape as above, different `errorCode` set | central-lab |

## Version segment

| Target | Path | Note |
|--------|------|------|
| CRF upload | `/api/1.00` | |
| dataset, subject | `/api/1.00` | |
| central-lab | `/api/{version}` | v1, v2 |

## Authentication

HTTP Basic Authentication (RFC 7617), verified by the gateway.

This API is stateless. There is no login or session step, so every request must
carry its credentials in the header.

```
Authorization: Basic {base64(clientId:clientSecret)}
```

Join the clientId and password issued to you with `:` and Base64-encode the
result (RFC 7235 4.2).

| Caution | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| Credential characters | Use ASCII only. A charset mismatch between encoding and decoding returns 401 |
| No line breaks | MIME-style encoders wrap every 76 characters and corrupt the header value |
| Every request | There is no session to authenticate once and reuse |

### Query string encoding

Encode parameters before sending them, but encode them **only once**. Passing an
already-encoded string back through a URI template turns `%40` into `%2540`, and
the value stops matching.

A `+` inside a value must be encoded as `%2B`. In a query string `+` means a
space, and RFC 3986 encoders may leave it as is, so `user+tag@example.com`
arrives as `user tag@example.com`.

This applies to `userId` (an email address) and `fileKey`.

| Symptom | Cause |
|---------|-------|
| 200 with an empty result | The value was encoded twice |
| Text after `+` in an email became a space | `+` was not encoded as `%2B` |

### txId

The unique identifier tying one transaction together from request to response.
**The client generates it as a UUID version 1** and sends it. 36 bytes max.

- **It is not a deduplication key.** Sending the same `txId` again is not
  rejected, so retrying a write applies it twice.
- **Do not sort by it.** Depending on the generator, the embedded timestamp is
  not monotonic.

CDMS API gateway host.
Contact your CRScube representative for the address of each region
(KR / JP / EU) and environment.

tags.name: crf
tags.description: CRF data upload from external EDC vendors.

tags.name: dataset
tags.description: SDTM dataset extraction: request, status lookup, and download.

tags.name: central-lab
tags.description:
Central Lab test data upload and lookup.

The response format and error-code scheme differ from the other areas. Status
codes are used differently too: a missing `FileKey` returns 401, and exceeding
the data buffer returns 413.

post.description:
Stores CRF items collected by an external system against a subject.

Processing runs as job creation → CRF data staging → upload execution, and a
failure at each stage maps to a different `GatewayError`.

**Server-side processing failures return HTTP 200 with `result` set to false
in the body.**

| Failure point | GatewayError | HTTP |
|---------------|--------------|-----:|
| Job initialization failed | `SERVER_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` | 200 |
| CRF data validation failed | `SERVER_VALIDATION_FAILED` | 200 |
| Save failed | `SERVER_SAVE_FAILED` | 200 |
| Data processing error | `SERVER_PROCESSING_FAILED` | 200 |

Do not judge success or failure from the HTTP status alone.

200.description: Upload succeeded, or failed during server-side processing. Use `result` to tell them apart.

errors: (2200) You do not have access to Study.

get.description:
Returns the SDTM domains that can be selected for extraction.

Two checks are performed.

1. System usage permission — `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (400) if missing
2. Dataset lookup permission — `FORBIDDEN` (400) if missing

**Both cases return HTTP 400**, not 403 or 404.

domains.description: Returns an empty array when there are no results.

post.description:
Creates an asynchronous extraction job and returns its job key.
Poll progress with `GET .../dataset/jobs/{jobKey}`, then download the result
from `/download` once it completes.

Validation runs in the following order, and each stage fails with a different
`errorCode`.

1. Usage permission — `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` / `FORBIDDEN` (400)
2. `codeType` and `fileType` parsing — `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (400)
3. Domain existence — `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (400)
4. NonCRF (Audit trail) mixed with other sources — `INVALID_REQUEST` (400)
5. `codeType` x `fileType` combination — `INVALID_REQUEST` (400)
6. Job already in progress — `UNABLE_OPERATE_STATUS` (**202**)

jobKey.description: Job key used for status lookup and download.

get.description:
Returns the current status of the job. The value is the display string below.

| Value | Meaning | Downloadable |
|-------|---------|--------------|
| `Initialization` | Initializing | x |
| `Progress` | In progress | x |
| `Continue` | Continuing | x |
| `Success` | Succeeded | O |
| `Fail` | Failed | O |

If the `jobKey` does not exist, or its status is none of the five values above,
the response is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (400).

This endpoint does not take `roleId` (the download endpoint requires it).

Streams the output file of a completed extraction job.

## When a download is possible

The job status must be **`Success` or `Fail`**. Calling this endpoint while the
status is `Initialization`, `Progress` or `Continue` returns **HTTP 202** with
`UNABLE_OPERATE_STATUS`. That is a 2xx, but it is a failure.

Even when the status qualifies, a missing output file returns
`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (400).

`Content-Type` is derived from the file extension.

post.description:
Registers a subject from an external system. The `txId` from the request is
echoed back in both success and failure responses, so the caller can trace the
transaction.

Validation runs in this order.

1. Site existence — `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` if missing (**400**, not 404)
2. Duplicate screening number — `CONFLICT` (409) if duplicated

`studyId` is case-insensitive.

Sends lab test results as JSON. The job ID (`fileKey`) is returned
immediately and processing continues asynchronously.

Poll progress with `GET /central-labs/{fileKey}`.

## Differences between v1 and v2

| Item | v1 | v2 |
|------|----|----|
| `txId` | optional | **required** |
| Error response | carried in `result` | **carried in `error`** |

This specification describes v2.

The `data` items you can send depend on the BUILDER > DCL > Central Lab
configuration. Use the **ID of each configured item as the JSON key**; items
that are not configured may be omitted.

200.description:
Accepted. Poll progress using the returned `fileKey`.
**The status is 200, not 201.**

get.description:
Returns the processing status of a submitted transaction (`fileKey`).

Processing has two stages, `validityCheck` (validation) and `crfSync` (eCRF
synchronization); their combination determines `message`. See the
`CentralLabProgressResult` schema for the full combination table.

Processing is complete when `validityCheck` is no longer `Progress`.

result.message: Only validated Central Lab data synced.

get.description:
Returns per-row success and failure details of the validation performed on
uploaded raw data. Use the `result` parameter to select only successful (`S`)
or only failed (`F`) rows.

For failed rows, the reason is carried in `MESSAGE`
(for example, "This subject doesn't exist. [Screening No.]").

A large result set triggers 413, so lower `rowCount` and call again.

200.description: Lookup succeeded. When there are no results, `datas` is `null` rather than an empty array.

get.description:
Returns per-row success and failure details of how validated data was applied
to the eCRF.

Each row carries `RESULT` (success or failure), `MESSAGE`, `TEAM`,
`INPUT_TIME` and so on.

200.description: Lookup succeeded. When there are no results, `datas` is `null`.

get.description:
Returns the Central Lab upload history for a study. Each row carries
`FILE_KEY`, `FILE_NAME`, `CHECK_RESULT` (validation), `SYNC_RESULT` (eCRF
synchronization), `MESSAGE` and `INPUT_TIME`.

Use the `FILE_KEY` obtained here to call the status and detail endpoints.

200.description: Lookup succeeded. When there are no results, `datas` is `null`.

datas.MESSAGE: 유효성 검사를 통과한 Central Lab 데이터만이 정상반영되었습니다.

gatewayBasicAuth.description:
External API client credentials (HTTP Basic).
**Verified by the API gateway.**

401 and 403 are therefore returned by the gateway, and their response format
differs from the other errors.

StudyId.name: studyId
StudyId.description:
Study identifier (Study ID).
The subject registration API uppercases the value, so lowercase input is
accepted.

JobKey.name: jobKey
JobKey.description:
Extraction job key. This is the `result.jobKey` value from the
`POST /api/1.00/studies/{studyId}/dataset/jobs` response.

UserIdQuery.name: userId
UserIdQuery.description:
User ID (email format). Used to determine access permission.

- Missing: 400 (`REQUIRED_PARAMETER`, "userId must not be blank")
- Unregistered value: 400 (`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, "userId does not exist.")

RoleIdQueryOptional.name: roleId
RoleIdQueryOptional.description:
Role ID. Used to determine access permission.

**It may be omitted for a user with a single role, but is required for a user
assigned two or more.** Omitting it then returns 400 (`REQUIRED_PARAMETER`,
"Role id must be specified."). An unregistered value returns 400
(`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, "roleId does not exist.").

RoleIdQueryRequired.name: roleId
RoleIdQueryRequired.description:
Role ID.

**Omitting it always returns 400.** Send it even for a user with only one role.

AcceptLanguage.name: Accept-Language
AcceptLanguage.description:
Response message language. When omitted, the language of the calling client is
used. Any value other than `ko`, `ja` or `zh` returns English.

CacheControl.name: Cache-Control
CacheControl.description: Cache directive. The recommended value is `max-age=0`.

CentralLabVersion.name: version
CentralLabVersion.description:
API version. Data upload and status lookup support both v1 and v2.
In v2, `txId` becomes required and errors are carried in `error` rather than
`result`.

CentralLabUserId.name: userId
CentralLabUserId.description:
User ID or email. Passing a user that does not exist returns 400 with the
errorCode `REQUIRED_PARAMETER` ("Required userId parameter 'User not exists'
is not present").

FileKey.name: fileKey
FileKey.description: Central Lab upload job identifier. This is the `result.fileKey` value from the `POST /central-labs` response.

PageNo.name: pageNo
PageNo.description: Page number. A malformed value returns 400 (`INVALID_PARAMETER`).

RowCount.name: rowCount
RowCount.description:
Rows per page. A large value triggers 413 (`Data buffer limit exceeded`), so
lower it and call again. A malformed value returns 400 (`INVALID_PARAMETER`).

ResultFlag.name: result
ResultFlag.description:
Which validation results to return. Only `S` (success) or `F` (failure) is
accepted; any other value returns 400 (`REQUIRED_PARAMETER`, "invalid
parameter (The result should be S or F.)").

GatewayBadRequest.description:
The request JSON is invalid, or validation failed.

| GatewayError | Where it occurs |
|--------------|-----------------|
| `CLIENT_BAD_REQUEST` | The request JSON could not be parsed |
| `CLIENT_VALIDATION_FAILED` | Field validation failed, or a `dataList` item failed validation |

Each entry in `error.errors` has the form `(code) message`, where the code is
derived from the HTTP status.

GatewayServerError.description:
Unclassified server error (`SERVER_UNKNOWN`).

Data processing errors are classified as `SERVER_PROCESSING_FAILED` and
returned with **HTTP 200**, so they do not appear here.

DatasetGetBadRequest.description:
Request failed. **This endpoint returns every error as 400.**
Missing resources and permission failures return 400 as well, not 404 or 403.

| errorCode | Cause |
|-----------|-------|
| `REQUIRED_PARAMETER` | `userId` or `roleId` missing or blank |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | No system usage permission, `jobKey` not found, file not found, domain not found |
| `FORBIDDEN` | No Dataset lookup permission |
| `INVALID_REQUEST` | The extraction server is unavailable |
| `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | Any other processing error (**status is still 400**) |

Note that `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` and `FORBIDDEN` return 400, not 404 or 403.

errorDetails: Do not have permission to query Dataset.

DatasetPostBadRequest.description:
Request failed. Unlike GET, the response includes `txId`.
The status still converges on 400.

| errorCode | Cause |
|-----------|-------|
| `REQUIRED_PARAMETER` | Required body field missing, or validation failed |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | Unknown domain, invalid `codeType` or `fileType`, no system usage permission |
| `FORBIDDEN` | No Dataset lookup permission |
| `INVALID_REQUEST` | Unsupported `codeType` / `fileType` combination, NonCRF (Audit trail) selected together with other sources, batch server not connected |
| `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | Any other processing error (**status is still 400**) |

errorDetails: The code type passed cannot output the file type.

DatasetJobInProgress.description:
**This is a failure, not a success.** An extraction job is already in progress,
so a new one could not be created.

This failure is returned as **202**. It is a 2xx, but `status` in the body is
`fail`.
**Do not treat it as success based on the status code alone.**

errorDetails: A job is in progress. Please try again after it's finished.

DatasetDownloadNotReady.description:
**This is a failure, not a success.** The job is not yet ready for download.

A download is only possible when the job status is `Success` or `Fail`.
Calling while the status is `Initialization`, `Progress` or `Continue` returns
this response.

The status code is 202, but this is **a failure despite being 2xx**, and
`status` in the body is `fail`.

errorDetails: The job is still in progress. Please request again after it is completed.

SubjectBadRequest.description:
Request failed. Several causes are grouped under this status code.

| errorCode | Cause |
|-----------|-------|
| `REQUIRED_PARAMETER` | Validation failure such as a missing `txId`, `userId` or `roleId` |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | The study has no such site (**not 404**) |
| `FORBIDDEN` | The user does not belong to a site allowed to register subjects |
| `FORBIDDEN` | The role lacks the `CREATE_SUBJECT` permission |
| `FAIL_SITE_CASES` | Site contract case limit exceeded |
| `FAIL_SITE_CASES` | The study uses the CONSENT solution — register from CONSENT instead |
| `FAIL_STUDY_CASES` | Study contract case limit exceeded |
| `DATA_PROCESSING_ERROR` | Data processing error |

Note that `FORBIDDEN` returns 400, not 403.

errorDetails: The team does not exist in the study.

value.message: The team does not exist in the study.

errorDetails: CREATE SUBJECT Privilege is not exist.

value.message: CREATE SUBJECT Privilege is not exist.

notInPermittedTeam.summary: Not a member of a site allowed to register

errorDetails: You do not belong to the team that has permission to register the user.

value.message: You do not belong to the team that has permission to register the user.

errorDetails: Cannot register more subjects. The number of registered subjects must not exceed the number of subjects in the contract (per site).

value.message: Subject cannot be registered greater than the number of contract cases for each site.

errorDetails: Cannot register more subjects. The number of registered subjects must not exceed the number of subjects in the contract.

value.message: Subject cannot be registered greater than the number of contract cases for the study.

errorDetails: This study is using the CONSENT solution. Please register subjects in the CONSENT.

value.message: This study is using the CONSENT solution. Please register subjects in the CONSENT.

SubjectConflict.description:
The screening number (`scrCode`) is already in use.

This is the only 4xx response in this area that is not a 400.

errorDetails: The screening code is already in use.

SubjectServerError.description:
Unhandled exception.

Unlike the `dataset` area, this area returns unclassified exceptions as 500.

TxIdReadFailure.description:
An error occurred while handling a POST request, and `txId` could not be read
again while building the error response. In that case the abbreviated response
below is returned.

If the `Accept` header contains `json` you get JSON; otherwise you get an HTML
error page. **Always send `Accept: application/json`.**

CrfUnauthorized.description:
Gateway authentication failed. **Returned by the gateway, but in the
`ApiResponse` format** — its shape differs from the other gateway errors.

CrfForbidden.description:
Gateway authorization denied. Use `errors` to distinguish the cause —
`User account is locked`, `User is disabled`, `User account has expired`,
`No study privilege`, `No api privilege`.

CrfNotFound.description: The requested URI does not exist.

CrfGatewayTimeout.description: The gateway could not reach the API server. The request may be retried.

GatewayUnauthorized.description:
Gateway authentication failed. The Authorization header is missing, or Basic
authentication failed.
**Returned by the gateway, not by the API server.**

GatewayForbidden.description:
Gateway authorization denied, because of account state or permissions.
**Returned by the gateway, not by the API server.**

Use `errorDetails` to distinguish the cause — `User account is locked`,
`User is disabled`, `User account has expired`, `No study privilege`,
`No api privilege`.

GatewayNotFound.description:
The requested URI does not exist. This includes calling a path that is not
registered as a gateway route.

GatewayTimeout.description: The gateway could not reach the API server. The request may be retried.

CentralLabBadRequest.description:
Invalid request parameter.

| errorCode | Cause |
|-----------|-------|
| `REQUIRED_PARAMETER` | `userId` or `result` missing, request body missing, unknown userId, `result` is neither S nor F |
| `INVALID_PARAMETER` | Malformed `pageNo` or `rowCount`, Study ID format mismatch |

Note that an unknown user is also reported as `REQUIRED_PARAMETER`.

The Study ID format mismatch message is localized according to
`Accept-Language`.

errorDetails: Required String parameter 'userId' is not present
Required userId parameter 'User not exists' is not present

CentralLabUnauthorized.description:
Authentication failure, or a permission or resource problem.

Three separate causes are grouped under this status code.

| errorCode | Cause |
|-----------|-------|
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | Authorization header missing, Basic authentication failed |
| `NO_PAGE_PERMISSION` | No read/write permission on the Lab menu |
| `NO_PAGE_PERMISSION` | FileKey not found |

**A missing FileKey returns 401, not 404.**

CentralLabForbidden.description:
No access permission for the study. The `errorCode` is `NO_PAGE_PERMISSION`,
the same as for 401; only the status code distinguishes the two.

errorDetails: Study is null.[UserId: khkim01, StudyId: K0102]

CentralLabPayloadTooLarge.description:
The result set exceeded the buffer limit. **Lower `rowCount` and call again.**

The status is 413, but the `errorCode` is `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`.

SuccessResponse.description:
Success response format for the dataset GET endpoints.
`status` is fixed to `success` and is always present.

result.description:
Endpoint-specific result. Depending on the operation this is either a
`{ "<key>": content }` object or the content itself.

FailResponse.description:
Failure response format for the dataset GET endpoints.
`message` and `error` are always present.

message.description:
User-facing message, localized to the requested language.
The wording may change without notice, so do not branch on it.

ExternalSuccessResponse.description:
Success response format that echoes the request `txId`.
Used by dataset extraction job creation (POST) and external subject
registration.

txId.description: Echoes back the transaction identifier supplied in the request body.

ExternalFailResponse.description: Failure response format corresponding to ExternalSuccessResponse.

txId.description:
The `txId` re-read from the request body. It is null when the body has no
`txId`. If the body cannot be read again, an abbreviated error response is
returned instead of this format.

ErrorDetail.description: Error detail. Both keys are always present.

errorDetails.description: Field-level validation failure reasons, domain exception messages, and the like. May be empty.

ErrorCode.description:
Error code.

**These do not map one-to-one to HTTP status codes.** The combinations actually
observed on the endpoints in this document are as follows.

| errorCode | Actual HTTP |
|-----------|------------:|
| `REQUIRED_PARAMETER` | 400 |
| `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 400 (not 404) |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 400 (not 403) |
| `INVALID_REQUEST` | 400 |
| `DATA_PROCESSING_ERROR` | 400 |
| `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | dataset 400 / subject 500 |
| `UNABLE_OPERATE_STATUS` | 202 |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 |

The enum lists every defined value. `FAIL_SITE_CASES`, `FAIL_STUDY_CASES` and
`FAIL_USER_CASES` are not observed on the endpoints covered here.

LegacyExceptionResponse.description:
Response from the global error handler. Exceptions not classified by
endpoint-specific error handling end up here.

If the `Accept` header contains `json`, the JSON below is returned with
HTTP 500; otherwise an HTML error page is returned.

state.description: A body field that is always `400`. It differs from the HTTP status code (500).

GatewayErrorCode.description:
Error codes returned by the gateway. This is a separate set from `ErrorCode`.

| Code | HTTP | Cause |
|------|-----:|-------|
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | No Authorization header / Basic authentication failed |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Account locked, disabled or expired; no study privilege; no API privilege |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Requested URI does not exist |
| `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | 500 | Server error |
| `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Could not reach the API server |

GatewayFailResponse.description:
Failure response returned by the gateway. It uses the same response format as
the dataset, subject and central-lab areas, but a different `errorCode` set.

txId.description: The `txId` from the request body. May be null if the request was rejected at the header stage.

ApiRequest.description:
CRF data upload request body.
`version`, `studyId` and `subjectId` are filled in by the server from the path
variables.

txId.description:
Transaction Id (UUID version 1). Echoed back in both success and error
responses. Generate a new one for every call.

userId.description: CDMS User ID (email). The user who entered the CRF.

reason.description: Reason for the change or transfer, recorded in the Audit Trail. Optional.

tranKey.description: Transaction key on the caller side.

dataList.description: CRF items to store. Each item is validated individually.

CrfData.description: Value of a single CRF item.

visitCode.description: Visit code. Must match the value configured in CDMS.

crfgrpCode.description:
CRF group code.
**If omitted or null, it is filled in automatically from the Item information.**

delFlag.description: Whether to delete. Deletes the item when true.

ApiResponse.description:
Common success and failure response for the gateway CRF API.
Server-side processing failures (`SERVER_*`) arrive with HTTP 200 and `result`
set to false. The error classification code is not included in the body.

`result` is always present.

txId.description: The `txId` from the request. May be empty if the request could not be parsed.

error.description: Populated only on failure. It is null in a success response.

errors.description: Detail list in the form `(code) message`.

GatewayError.description:
Error classification code. It is not included in the body; it surfaces through
the HTTP status and the code prefix in `error.errors`.

| Code | HTTP | Message |
|------|------|---------|
| CLIENT_BAD_REQUEST | 400 | Request JSON is invalid |
| CLIENT_VALIDATION_FAILED | 400 | Validation failed |
| CLIENT_NO_AUTHORIZATION | 401 | No Authorization header |
| CLIENT_UNAUTHORIZED | 401 | Invalid Authorization header |
| SERVER_INITIALIZATION_FAILED | 200 | Fail to initialize |
| SERVER_VALIDATION_FAILED | 200 | Invalid CRF data |
| SERVER_SAVE_FAILED | 200 | Failed to save |
| SERVER_PROCESSING_FAILED | 200 | Data processing error |
| SERVER_UNKNOWN | 500 | Unknown error |

txId.description: Transaction identifier. Echoed back in both success and failure responses.

userId.description: ID of the user requesting the extraction.

roleId.description: Role ID of the requesting user.

domainList.description:
Domain IDs to extract. Use the `domainId` values returned by
`/dataset/domains`. The server uppercases them before matching, and a single
unknown value returns `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (400).

The NonCRF (Audit trail) domain cannot be selected together with other sources
(`INVALID_REQUEST`).

CodeType.description:
How code values are represented. Accepts **either the enum name or an alias**,
and aliases are case-insensitive. A value matching neither returns
`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (400, "Code Type is not appropriate.").

| Enum name | Alias |
|-----------|-------|
| `CODE` | `code` |
| `LABEL` | `label` |
| `CODE_LABEL` | `code/label` |
| `SPLIT_CODE_LABEL` | `code+label` |

For the constraints against `fileType`, see the `FileType` schema.

FileType.description:
Output file format. Enum names are accepted case-insensitively.
A value that does not match returns `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`
(400, "File Type is not appropriate.").

## Constraints against `codeType`

A violation returns `INVALID_REQUEST` (400,
"The code type passed cannot output the file type.").

| codeType | Allowed fileType |
|----------|------------------|
| `CODE` | all (XPT, SAS, ACCESS, EXCEL, CSV) |
| `LABEL` | EXCEL, CSV |
| `CODE_LABEL` | EXCEL, CSV, SAS(*) |
| `SPLIT_CODE_LABEL` | SAS(*) |

(*) Only when `domainList` consists **solely of CRF sources**.
Mixing in other sources rejects the SAS combination.

Domain.description:
An SDTM domain available for extraction.
All three fields are always present.

domainId.description: Domain ID. This is the value you put in `domainList` of an extraction request.

source.description:
Data source category.
The NonCRF (Audit trail) source cannot be extracted together with other sources.

DocumentStatus.description:
Extraction job status. The **display string** below is returned verbatim.

| Value | Downloadable |
|-------|--------------|
| `Initialization` | x |
| `Progress` | x |
| `Continue` | x |
| `Success` | O |
| `Fail` | O |

A download is only possible from `Success` or `Fail`, which means
**a failed job can also be downloaded**. If no output file exists, however, the
response is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (400, "File does not exist.").

If the `jobKey` does not exist, or the status is none of the five values above,
the response is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (400, "JobKey does not exist.").

ExternalSubjectCreateRequest.description: Subject registration request for external systems.

txId.description:
Transaction identifier. Echoed back in both success and failure responses.
A blank value returns 400 (`txId must not be blank`).

userId.description:
ID of the user performing the registration.
A blank value returns 400 (`userId must not be blank`).

roleId.description:
Role ID of the user performing the registration.
A blank value returns 400 (`roleId must not be blank`).

scrCode.description: Screening number. A value already in use returns 409 (`CONFLICT`).

ExternalSubjectCreateResponse.description: Registration result. Only `subjectId` is returned, and the key is always present.

CentralLabUploadRequest.description:
Central Lab test result upload request. The job ID (`fileKey`) is returned
immediately and processing continues asynchronously.

Each object in `data` uses the **ID configured under BUILDER > DCL > Central
Lab as its JSON key**. IDs not shown in the example below can also be sent if
they are configured, and items not configured in BUILDER may be omitted.

txId.description:
Transaction Id (UUID version 1).
**Optional in v1, required in v2.**

CentralLabDataItem.description:
A single lab result. The keys are the COL_IDs configured in BUILDER.
Below is the full list of COL_IDs documented; which ones are usable depends on
the study configuration. Keys not listed here can also be sent when they are
configured, so `additionalProperties` is left open.

STUDY_ID.description: Study ID (CONST). A value that does not match the configured format returns 400 (`INVALID_PARAMETER`).

BIRTH_DATE.description: Date of Birth (DATE). YYYYMMDD | YYYY-MM-DD | YYYY/MM/DD

VALUE.description: Analysis result (CHAR). The documented examples use both numbers and text.

LOWER_LIMIT.description: Reference Range Lower Limit (CHAR or NUMBER)

UPPER_LIMIT.description: Reference Range Upper Limit (CHAR or NUMBER)

fileKey.description:
The created job key. Use it to poll progress and validation results.
The documented example is a string (`"3850993"`).

CentralLabProgressResult.description:
Processing status of the upload job. The combination of `validityCheck` and
`crfSync` determines `message`.

| validityCheck | crfSync | Example message |
|---------------|---------|-----------------|
| Progress | Waiting | - |
| Success | Success | Validation and data reflection were completed successfully. |
| Success | Partially Successful | Validation passed, but only 1 out of 2 data was reflected. |
| Partially Successful | Success | Only validated central Lab data was reflected successfully. |
| Partially Successful | Partially Successful | Only 1 of 2 validated Central Lab data was successfully reflected. |
| Partially Successful | Fail | None of validated Central Lab data can be reflected. |
| Fail | - | No validated Central Lab data. |

fileKey.description: The documented examples contain both strings and numbers.

crfSync.description: eCRF synchronization status. A failure is shown as `-`.

message.description: Message corresponding to the status combination.
message.example: Only validated Central Lab data synced.

CentralLabGridResult.description:
Grid-shaped result shared by the detail and list endpoints.
`columns` varies with the per-study BUILDER configuration, and the keys of
`datas` correspond to the keys of `columns`.

columns.description:
Mapping from column ID to display name. The composition varies with the
per-study Central Lab column configuration.

datas.description: Query result. **When there are no results this is `null`, not an empty array.**

CentralLabErrorCode.description:
Error codes for the Central Lab API. This is a different set from the
`ErrorCode` used elsewhere.

| Code | Observed HTTP | Cause |
|------|--------------:|-------|
| `REQUIRED_PARAMETER` | 400 | Required parameter missing, unknown userId |
| `INVALID_PARAMETER` | 400 | Malformed `pageNo` or `rowCount`, Study ID format mismatch |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Authorization header missing, Basic authentication failed |
| `NO_PAGE_PERMISSION` | 401 / 403 | No Lab read/write permission, FileKey not found, no study access permission |
| `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | 413 | Data buffer limit exceeded |

**`NO_PAGE_PERMISSION` appears under both 401 and 403.**
Permission and FileKey problems are documented as 401; study access problems
as 403.

CentralLabFailResponse.description: Failure response format for the Central Lab API.

txId.description: Present only in some error responses, and often `null`.
